span: Respondent No.1 sent the statutory demand notice under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act
why: Facts stating that a demand notice was sent; no ruling on whether notice is a pre-condition.

span: Since no payment was forthcoming pursuant to the two statutory demand notices
why: Facts of the complaints; notice is mentioned only as a fact.

span: Secondly, a demand of payment ought to have been made by the presenter of the cheque to the issuer
why: Headnote holding lists a demand for payment (notice) as one of three essential conditions for invoking s.138, and says the cause of action arises only after failure to pay on receipt of the notice.

span: a presumption under Section 139 of the Negotiable Instruments Act in favour of the holder would be attracted
why: About the s.139 presumption and burden of proof.

span: Section 138 of the NI Act being penal in nature has to be strictly construed
why: Headnote on strict construction, drawer liability and the meaning of 'account maintained by him'; nothing on demand notice.

span: has refused to quash the complaint filed against the appellant
why: Procedural background of an appeal against refusal to quash a s.138/141 complaint.
